name: client-audit
what: Every step of a full client audit of a live site (audit-live), in one list that start.mjs and `omnikom seo run` both read. Steps marked needsBrowser owner, needsAi or needsPerson are never run by a script: the runner lists them as WAITING with their brief, an agent or the owner writes their outputs, and the next resume picks them up.

conventions.lastLine: A step that exits 3 prints `BLOCKED: <what> | unblocks: <what would>`; one that exits 4 prints `SKIPPED: <reason>`. The runner quotes that line and never invents a reason.
conventions.done: exit 0 in the run log AND every evidence path exists, is not empty, and was written after the step started; an input newer than the evidence makes the step stale. A run adopts existing evidence only when no input is newer (for a person approval, an input with the approved copy's own bytes is not newer), its newest file is within maxAgeDays (null: no limit; 0: nothing from before this run) and no evidence pattern holds only BLOCKED records.
conventions.hits: Two steps that hit the same host never run at the same time. pace is informational: the script enforces it.
conventions.scriptPaths: Relative to the skill folder. `repo:` means relative to the Omnikom repository root.

vars.key: the run's key: the site's url, or profile:<client-slug> for a client with no site (then {url} has no value and {host} is the slug)
vars.client: the client slug (clients/<slug>/ in the Omnikom repo)
vars.data: the run's data folder; until row R3 the skill folder

stations.what: the site itself: reach, snapshot, speed, the checks
who the business is, what it sells, the seeds
where the site stands in Google and Bing
the map, the listing, the directories
the report and the client's copy

steps.what: which free sources and keys are connected; the latest Common Crawl release
US vantage (Sacramento) verified before any capture

polite snapshot of the site, raw HTML and rendered in real Chrome, phone speed in the lab (a snapshot younger than 7 days is reused; either way snapshots/latest.json says which one this run handed on)
steps.pace: 1 request per 4 s, robots.txt obeyed, a 429 waits 90 s once then stops

steps.what: Google's PageSpeed test, phone and desktop, three runs each: every run's raw answer is kept and the median is recorded (medianOf says how many runs it is a median of)
steps.pace: 2 s between calls, 31 s between two runs of the same page (Google may answer a repeat within about 30 s from one analysis)

steps.what: real-visitor speed from the Chrome UX Report, for the page and its origin on phones and desktops; NO DATA (too little traffic) is a result, not a failure
steps.pace: 1 s between calls

steps.what: the shipgate checker by program: the measurable rules judge the snapshot and write the root causes, no model
who the client is (business.json): name, address, phone, services, service area, market
the business definition is signed by the head's written rule (the owner's ruling of 2026-11-21), including serviceArea (local-grid refuses without it: work order 40)
steps.brief: The head's stamp is written by rule (the owner's ruling of 2026-11-21, scripts/sign-off-rule.json): every owner-only field that has a value and was not answered by the owner is stamped delegated, then approve.mjs signs. A person is asked only for an owner-only field with no value (the step prints one NEEDS-INPUT line naming each): ask the owner as pickable options, write the answer as {"value":..., "answeredBy":"owner"} in intake-answers.json and run intake again. A field the owner answered himself is never touched. His own signature stays possible: `node scripts/approve.mjs {key} business --by "<owner>" --cwd {skill}`.

steps.what: each service-area city's centre (latitude, longitude, source page, date) read from the coordinates of the city's Wikipedia page, one polite request per city; a city with no coordinates is BLOCKED by name
steps.pace: one request per city, 250 ms apart, a descriptive User-Agent

steps.what: search seeds proposed from the business's own words and places; nothing fetched
the seeds are signed by the head's written rule (the owner's ruling of 2026-11-21) before any call is spent on them
steps.brief: The head's stamp is written by rule (the owner's ruling of 2026-11-21, scripts/sign-off-rule.json): approve.mjs checks the seeds and signs. A person is asked only when approve.mjs refuses them (the step prints one NEEDS-INPUT line with its reason): fix research/seeds.json (run research-seeds.mjs again) and run this step again. His own signature stays possible: `node scripts/approve.mjs {key} seeds --by "<owner>" --cwd {skill}`.

steps.what: Bing keyword estimates and related keywords for every seed, plain and with the city and state; the client's own site statistics are BLOCKED until the client adds us as a user in Bing Webmaster Tools (the estimates go on)
steps.pace: the script's own call cap (60)

steps.what: the client's own search data; BLOCKED until the client adds us as a user
the research run's plan and the capture requests for the owner's browser (dry run: nothing fetched)
the research plan's cost (a number of requests to free sources; money is always 0) is signed by the head's written rule when it is 150 or fewer; above 150 the run stops for the owner
steps.brief: The head's stamp is written by rule (the owner's ruling of 2026-11-21, scripts/sign-off-rule.json): a plan of 150 requests or fewer is signed through approve.mjs research-cost. Above 150 the step prints one NEEDS-INPUT line with the total, the ceiling and the owner's own command and signs nothing: the owner signs it himself (`node scripts/approve.mjs {key} research-cost --by "<owner>" --cwd {skill}`), then run this step again.

steps.what: Google results pages: every buyer search, the brand searches, each service + city, with the AI answer, People Also Ask and related searches
steps.pace: one page at least 45 s apart; stop at the first robot check
steps.brief: In the owner's Edge, open each Google request in capture-requests.json plus the brand searches (business name, short name, domain) and each service + city. Save each page in the serp capture format with its footer location (a location outside the market makes it a national baseline, not local).

steps.what: Bing results pages for the same buyer and brand searches
steps.pace: one page at least 45 s apart; stop at the first robot check
steps.brief: In the owner's Edge, the same buyer searches and the brand searches on bing.com; save each in the serp capture format with engine bing.

steps.what: index coverage: site: searches on Google and Bing, and whether each service has an indexed page
steps.pace: one page at least 45 s apart
steps.brief: site:{host} on Google and Bing: record the result count shown and the addresses listed; then for each service, whether a page for it is listed.

steps.what: index captures become counts: the pages each engine lists for site:<host>, and which services have a listed page
autocomplete suggestions on Google and Bing for each service + city and the brand
steps.pace: type slowly, never press Enter, 45 s between seeds
steps.brief: Type each seed slowly into the search box without pressing Enter and save the list shown, in the format at the top of scripts/research-autocomplete.mjs.

steps.what: autocomplete captures become sourced demand estimates and new queries
Google Trends interest by region for each service: the state among states, the metro within the state
steps.pace: one page at least 45 s apart
steps.brief: trends.google.com, past 12 months, one service per page: the country's region table (the client's state and its rank) and the state's metro table (the client's metro). Save the tables with the address read.

steps.what: Trends region tables become ranks: the client's state among the states and its metro, per service
The AI assistants' two fixed texts are built by program from the signed seeds: one prompt of buyer questions per place and a follow-up by name; the first text never holds the business's own name
The two built texts are frozen as they are, with the run's own record that it froze them; every later send is checked against this lock
args: the audit run: both texts are built by program from the signed seeds and the two fixed prompt files

steps.what: ChatGPT, Perplexity and Gemini (only if signed in) are asked in the work browser, one assistant at a time: the first text and the follow-up in one chat each, at one fixed pace; a human check rings the owner and waits; every reply is saved whole and asked.json says what happened to each assistant
steps.pace: one tab and one assistant at a time, typing and reading at the rates and the wait between assistants of the pace block of work-browser-engines.json, each assistant asked once, no retry

steps.what: The saved replies are counted by program, no model: per assistant and question whether the business is listed, who is listed instead and which sources are named; writes the files the import reads

AI answers beyond Google become counts per engine: questions, how often the business is named (checked against the text), who is named instead, which sources are cited; a blocked engine is a BLOCKED row
imports the captures and runs clustering, competitors, winners, citations and AI citations; writes targets.json
steps.pace: competitor sites: 1 request per 4 s per host

steps.what: the target list is well formed and every target is sourced
a grid of points around each service-area city and the capture requests for Maps
Google Maps by viewport: the client's own listing, and each service at the city centre and the grid points
steps.pace: one page at least 45 s apart; stop at the first robot check
steps.brief: Google Maps ranks by the map's viewport, not by IP (work order 40: a browser outside the market cannot localize web results). Open https://www.google.com/maps/search/<service>/@<lat>,<lng>,14z for each point in the grid requests, and record the results list in the local-pack format with method "maps-viewport" and viewport {lat, lng, zoom} read back from the page's address after the list has loaded. Then search the business's own name: record its profile (rating, reviews, category, photos), or that none exists.

steps.what: competitor sites read the way a crawler reads them: words, sitemap, schema, FAQ, llms.txt, AI crawler access
steps.pace: 1 request per 4 s per host, robots.txt obeyed, the first 403/429 stops the host

steps.what: the competitor list is signed by the head's written rule (the owner's ruling of 2026-11-21): national, local lenders and brokers, aggregators, before authority compares against it
steps.brief: The head's stamp is written by rule (the owner's ruling of 2026-11-21, scripts/sign-off-rule.json): approve.mjs checks {pewp}/research/competitors-proposed.json and signs. No step of this manifest writes that file: `node scripts/competitors-discover.mjs {key} --cwd {skill}` does, from what the discovery agents found (stages/overhaul.md step 4); the step is BLOCKED until it is there. A person is asked only when approve.mjs refuses the list (the step prints one NEEDS-INPUT line with its reason): show the owner {pewp}/research/competitors-proposed.md, local ones first, as pickable options, fix the rows and run this step again. His own signature stays possible: `node scripts/approve.mjs {key} competitors --by "<owner>" --cwd {skill}`.

steps.what: linking domains for the client and its competitors from the free Common Crawl web graph
steps.pace: downloads a release once and caches it; check 15 GB free first

steps.what: anchor text and follow/nofollow of the links from the referring domains to the client and its competitors, read from Common Crawl's own copies of the pages (no referring site is requested)
steps.pace: one request per 3 s to the Common Crawl data host, hard cap 600 requests (the cluster.idx download counts as one), about 30 to 40 minutes; responses are cached so a re-run costs nothing

exit.3: BLOCKED: no authority.json, free disk under 15 GB, or the 24 h Common Crawl stop file is in force (it prints until when)

steps.what: the link gap ranked into places to earn links, mentions and citations
a polite read-only visit to each link opportunity: indexable, follow or nofollow, free or paid
steps.pace: 1 request per 4 s per host

steps.what: Maps captures become a per-point position table and a share of local voice
the business's listings on directories (Yelp, BBB, Bing Places, Apple Maps, Manta, Yellow Pages and the market's own) for name, address and phone
steps.pace: one page at least 45 s apart per site
steps.brief: Search each directory for the business by name and city, read only. Record the name, address and phone it shows, or that it is not listed, in the citations.json format at the top of scripts/local-nap.mjs.

steps.what: the local suite: Business Profile, map-pack positions, NAP consistency, review gap
reviews and complaints: Google reviews, BBB (rating, accreditation, complaints), Trustpilot, Yelp; for the client and the top local competitors
steps.pace: one page at least 45 s apart per site
steps.brief: Read only, no login. Per site and business: the rating, review count, newest review date, complaint count and accreditation, or 'not listed'. Never copy a reviewer's name.

steps.what: review captures become ratings, review counts, newest review and complaints per business and site (no reviewer names ever stored)
public social profiles: YouTube, TikTok, Instagram, LinkedIn (company and people), Facebook; counts, newest post, the link to the site
steps.pace: one page at least 45 s apart per site
steps.brief: Public pages only, nothing clicked beyond reading. Per profile: followers, posts or videos (with Shorts counted: work order 40), views, the newest post date, and where its link goes (open the link and record the status the visitor sees). A login wall means BLOCKED.

steps.what: social captures become followers, posts, newest post, active or not, and whether the profile's link works
ads the client and its top competitors run: Google Ads Transparency Center and the Meta Ad Library
steps.pace: one page at least 45 s apart
steps.brief: adstransparency.google.com and facebook.com/ads/library, US: per advertiser, whether ads are running, how many, since when, and the formats. Read only.

steps.what: ad library captures become running or not, ad count and since when, per advertiser and library
Reddit mentions of the business and of its services in its city
steps.pace: 1 request per 7 s; the first 429/403 stops it (without a token Reddit answers 403: work order 40)

steps.what: the client's profile: what every station gathered, pooled in one file, and the internal sheet of what was not gathered

the judge: one headless model reads the client's profile and writes the report's analysis as JSON in a fixed shape, which the number guard checks (the model is asked once, and a second time only after a refusal)
the six-question report in plain words, every number sourced
a fresh agent that did not write the report re-checks every number against its source
steps.pace: re-measures politely: 1 request per 4 s
steps.brief: A fresh agent with no part in the report: re-measure what can be re-measured (PageSpeed median of 3, served and rendered counts two ways, page statuses), re-read every capture cited, and write one row per claim with the verdict MATCH, MISMATCH, OVERSTATED, NO SOURCE or UNPROVEN.

steps.what: the client's report of 6 to 8 pages, printed from the judge's analysis: one html and one numbers sheet, every number read from a file of the run through the pointers the number guard checked (always a draft: a final copy needs a sign-off)
the copy printed to a PDF with headless Chrome on the shared profile, and the print checked (page count, no blank page)
